title: Physical Backups & Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR)
description: Archive Write-Ahead Logs (WAL) continuously and restore the database to the exact second before a disaster occurred.

data.text: While logical backups (`pg_dump`) export SQL commands, enterprise disaster recovery relies on **Continuous Archiving and Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR)**. By combining a base physical backup (`pg_basebackup`) with a stream of archived WAL segments, you can restore your database to any exact timestamp.

data.caption: Point-In-Time Recovery Mechanism
data.definition:
flowchart LR
    A[Base Backup: Sunday 00:00] --> B[WAL Stream: Sun - Wed]
    B --> C{Accidental DROP TABLE: Wed 14:15:00}
    A --> D[Replay WAL to Target]
    B --> D
    D -->|recovery_target_time = 14:14:59| E[Clean Database Restored Without Data Loss]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PITR combines a physical base backup with continuous WAL segment archiving.
Allows rolling back to the exact second prior to accidental data loss.
Tools like `pgBackRest` and `WAL-G` automate enterprise PITR to S3/GCS.
